title: Field diary: fourteen days of weather and wiring
intro: Short entries from the coastal station, written at the end of each day and edited as little as possible.

add_paragraph.heading: Day 1
add_paragraph.text: Arrived at 16:00. The station is colder inside than out. The generator starts on the fourth attempt. We sleep before unpacking.

items_of_the_timeline.timeline_item_text: Masts raised, cables run, the first calibration abandoned at dusk.
Four clear days. Sampling runs to schedule; the data looks boring, which is the goal.
Gusts to 60 km/h. One mast down, repaired with spares and stubbornness.
Two days of packing, one of waiting for the boat.

add_image.image_alt: The station building in flat grey light
add_image.image_caption: Day 6. The light never quite arrived.

add_paragraph.heading: Day 9
add_paragraph.text: The wind took the upper mast at 03:40. Nobody heard it. We found it in the morning, half in the grass, still logging. The instrument survived; the bracket did not.

add_special_note.heading: What the diary is for
add_special_note.text: Not for publication, mostly. It is the record of the things that do not fit in a dataset — the reason a sample is missing, the mood of a team, the day the weather changed the plan.
